newsitem.title: USA: U.S. blue chips barely changed, Nasdaq slightly up.
newsitem.headline: U.S. blue chips barely changed, Nasdaq slightly up.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average wavered in morning trading on Thursday, unwilling to hold either gains or losses for very long.
Traders and analysts said stocks continued to watch the bond market for rising yields and any signs of concern about possible future interest rate hikes.
The Dow Jones industrial average was up 3.43 points at 7361, after finishing down on Wednesday. Nasdaq was up about three points at around 1413.
The long bond provided some support to share prices, up 9/32 at a 7.01 percent yield.
One trader said the stock market looked tired at these levels, unsure of what its next step would be.
Peter Coolidge, senior equity trader at Brean Murray & Co, said the market was experiencing healthy periods of consolidation followed by recovery, with buyers adding to positions on price dips.
"The market continues to march higher," he said. "The volume has slowed a little bit from recent days but the trend is higher. With each consolidation, the market comes back."
Advancing issues outnumbered declining issues on the New York stock exchange by 11 to nine.
